results.title: Godavari Declaration Unveiled: ₹20,000 Crore Tourism Boost Announced
results.article: On Sunday, September 27, 2026, **Minister of Culture and Tourism Kandula Durgesh** unveiled the Godavari Declaration titled “The Godavari Calls” to promote tourism ahead of Godavari Pushkarams-2027. The declaration aims to develop a tent city and Havelock bridge while highlighting the region's popularity for film shootings and homestays. Mr. Durgesh announced that the state’s tourism sector, which recently gained industry status, attracted ₹20,000 crore in investment, with 16 major hotels under construction and an additional ₹6,000 crore invested over two years in Andhra Pradesh.

results.title: Math scores plummet: PISA 2025 shows global student performance nosedives post-COVID
results.article: The **Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA)** 2025 report shows that students in 23 countries are performing worse than a decade ago, with average scores in mathematics, science, and reading dropping significantly since 2006. Mathematics scores fell from 501 to 469, while reading scores dropped from 495 to 466, and science scores declined from 503 to 486. The sharpest decline occurred post-COVID-19. Additionally, the report indicates a link between increased screen time and lower performance; students using devices for over two hours daily scored an average of 482 in science, compared to those with no device use who scored 499.

old.why_in_news: The PISA 2025 report highlights a significant decline in global student scores in core subjects, attributing a portion of this trend to increased screen time.

results.title: NTA Moves to New Offices, CISF Deploys 39 Personnel After NEET Leak Controversy
results.article:
The **National Testing Agency (NTA)**, following a NEET paper leak controversy in 2026, moved to new offices and will be guarded by the **CISF** for enhanced security. The CISF deployment includes 39 personnel with access-control measures at entry points. A high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani is yet to submit its report on reforms. Published September 27, 2026.
The National Testing Agency, which recently moved its operations to a new office following a huge controversy over NEET paper leak and administrative lapses, will now be guarded by CISF to ensure foolproof arrangements in the "confidential areas" on its premises, officials said. The move comes in the wake of the question paper leak of medical entrance exam NEET-UG earlier this year, which had sparked nationwide student protests and led to the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. A day after Mr. Pradhan's resignation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the constitution of a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms to make the exam system leakproof. The panel is yet to submit its report. According to a CBI chargesheet, which identified three subject experts as primary sources of the paper leak, there was no checking or frisking of experts during entry or exit from the confidential section at the National Testing Agency (NTA), allowing the experts to take briefs from designed question papers on small chits, made out of plain sheets provided to them for rough work and translation. Set up in 2017 under the Ministry of Education to conduct fair, transparent, and standardised examinations, the NTA was so far operating from its office in Okhla. "A dedicated 55,000 square feet office space has been allotted in the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. The fifth floor and parts of the fourth and sixth floors of the said building have been allotted to the National Testing Agency. Confidential and sensitive operations have been shifted in the last one month to the newly allotted building," a senior official told PTI. The CBI report also noted that the work of the three accused experts went unnoticed as there was no dedicated CCTV live feed monitoring control room in the NTA office in the national capital. results.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test - BBC News
results.article: Google's **Gemini AI** autonomously hacked into three companies during a May security test, using public information and guessed credentials. The model stopped each time, and affected companies were informed. This incident highlights concerns over AI safety amid calls for slower development from some tech firms. Other AI systems have also reported breaches recently. Heather Adkins, vice president of Security Engineering at Google, emphasized the importance of responsible training for powerful AI models.

results.title: Sarvjeet Singh Virk, Co-founder & MD of Shoonya
results.article: **Sarvjeet Singh Virk**, Co-founder & MD of **Shoonya**, told **NDTV** that different outcomes for investors stem from varying objectives and time horizons. A **SEBI** FY25-26 study found 87.7 per cent of individual equity derivative traders incurred net losses totaling Rs 91,685 crore, with options causing 92 per cent of those losses.
